scoring_justification: Full recompute by re-running NEGF not feasible in verifier; score headline power factor against paper-reported gold and confirm structural trends (monotonicity, single peak, ordering) plus internal consistency between raw data and peak summary.

hidden_assets.purpose: Paper-reported headline power factor: PF=33 mW/(m·K²) at Cd=10%, Lg=210nm
hidden_assets.generation_method: Digitized from paper text: 'PF ... shows a maximum value of 33 mW/(m K²) at Lg=210 nm'
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: Direct quote from paper's abstract and Fig.4 caption; confirmed by Fig.4 data.

hidden_assets.purpose: Ordinal relationship of optimum lengths: Lg_opt(10%) > Lg_opt(15%) > Lg_opt(20%)
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Paper Fig.5 and text: 'both <PF>max and optimum Lg decrease monotonically as Cd increases'
hidden_assets.generation_method: Derived from paper conclusion, not specific numbers.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: The qualitative trend is stated explicitly in the paper.

outputs.description: Ensemble-averaged length-dependent thermoelectric properties (conductivity, Seebeck coefficient, power factor) for each edge-disorder concentration. The hidden checker will compare these simulated values against digitized reference data from the paper and check structural trends.

Maximum power factor and the ribbon length at which it occurs for each edge-disorder concentration. Verified against paper-reported numbers and the trend that optimum length decreases with increasing disorder.

output_contract.notes: The scoring uses a combination of reference matching against hidden digitized values and structural trend checks (monotonicity, peak existence, ordering). Tolerances account for implementation differences and sampling noise. The load-bearing step_03 ensures the agent must genuinely execute the NEGF simulations.
